analysis: Docs-only change to docs/architecture/inference.md; no code or control changes are in the supplied evidence. The additions at head 25-171 document unregistered, non-production Nemotron Super local paths. These are a builder and binding, an image binding, an optional loopback HTTP hook (default absent, authenticated, 429 on overload), a prefix-cache checkpoint bank, and opt-in MTP speculation. The doc says no model is registered, no HTTP route is exposed and no production caller installs the hook. Relevant threats are T-041 (prefix cache, TTFT oracle, resident RAM versus the 'no production RAM tier' statement, unscoped local scope), T-007 and T-056 (output correctness is not established; the doc says full-checkpoint quality is unmeasured), and TB-007 (decrypted prompts in process memory and GPU memory). The doc describes media charged for admission before decode and the rejection of non-PNG/JPEG data URIs, which is consistent with the existing media caps. The one-line change at head 868-869 says multimodal template fixtures run under a 'shared media discovery policy' instead of `vision_config`. That policy lives in model-registry.md, which was not supplied, so its security meaning is unverified. The next pass should check whether the Swift sources named in the doc exist in other PRs and whether DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 also gates DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY. It should also check that a production caller cannot register this owner without a coordinator-derived cacheSalt.

findings.detail: The new doc text describes an opt-in resident recurrent checkpoint bank (DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=1) in which text requests are submitted with prefix caching on and a 'local unscoped cache scope'. T-041 states that production has no resident-RAM prefix cache or tier composition. It also states that cache scope is coordinator-authored from account, model build and prompt contract. The new owner has no per-account scope and uses a different env gate from the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch. If the loopback HTTP hook (NemotronSuperLocalImageHTTP) or a later production caller serves multiple clients, they share one cache. A client could then use a TTFT hit/miss timing oracle against another client's prefixes. The doc says no production caller installs the hook, so this is not an active regression. T-041 should record the new tier and its scope assumptions before any registration or route is added. The review could not check whether DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 also disables this bank.
findings.title: Threat model lacks coverage for the new resident-RAM, unscoped prefix cache in the Nemotron Super local owner
